Record: Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification reports: DOI 10.69558/2026004, date 2026, venue 2. Open Source Hardware Konferenz 2025.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification reports: type proceedings-article, publisher.username Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft (HTWD), Dresden, citation count 0.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification reports: authors given: Erfan; family: Sotoodeh Nia Korrani; sequence: first; role: role: author; vocabulary: crossref.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification states in its own abstract: This paper presents an open-source hardware (OSH) solution for spectral color detection targeting soil classification and mineral identification.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification states in its own abstract: Traditional methods for these tasks, such as visual comparison with Munsell soil color charts, are highly subjective and prone to human error, while laboratory-grade spectrometers are cost-prohibitive for widespread field deployment.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification states in its own abstract: Although recent commercial portable sensors like the Nix Pro have improved in field analysis, their high cost (approximately $300) remains a significant barrier to adoption for educators, researchers, and practitioners.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification states in its own abstract: Our system addresses this gap by integrating a TCS3200 sensor, ATmega328P microcontroller, and multi-spectral LEDs (visible/IR) on a single-layer PCB with production costs under $100.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification states in its own abstract: Key innovations include: (1) hybrid classification algorithms combining RGB, IR (850nm/940nm), and temporal parameters achieving 95% accuracy; (2) signal settling time measurement as a novel indicator for material density; (3) modular design compatible with Arduino ecosystems.
The record for Low-Cost Open-Source Spectral Data-Based Color Detection Board for Soil and Mineral Classification states in its own abstract: Validated on 120 soil/mineral samples, the board reduces costs by 70% compared to dedicated portable spectrophotometers like Nix Pro while maintaining laboratory-grade precision.
